frequency_question: How often do major energy permitting and infrastructure reform bills successfully become law within a single congressional session given the presence of visible advance signals (such as committee hearings and bipartisan bill introductions)?
membership_rule: Includes major federal legislative vehicles explicitly aimed at reforming energy permitting, transmission, or fossil/renewable infrastructure approvals. Excludes standard annual appropriations bills and narrow non-controversial technical corrections.

cases.name: Energy Independence and Security Act of 2007
Energy Policy Modernization Act attempts (114th Congress)
Energy Act of 2020 (Division of Omnibus Appropriations)
Manchin Permitting Reform Bill Attempts (117th/118th Congress)

coverage_note: 5 major legislative cycles identified; captures the modern era of polarized congressional energy negotiations.
known_gaps: Excludes minor rider attachments included in must-pass defense authorization bills (NDAA) that partially touched permitting.
skeleton: Major energy reform push cycles in Congress since 1995: 5 major distinct legislative pushes identified, out of which 3 successfully resulted in enacted major energy reform packages containing permitting or infrastructure provisions.
multiplier: 3 hits out of 5 distinct major push cycles
validity_reason: Bound to the current congressional structural dynamics and polarization levels, which reset with each new two-year congressional term.
